signals.title: NOK/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: NOK leads G10 performance over the past week with an average gain of +0.927% across two pairs, while JPY lags as the weakest currency at -0.371% across seven pairs. That produces a 1.297% leader-to-laggard spread, well above the 1.20% critical threshold. The fundamental divergence is anchored by monetary policy: Norges Bank policy rate sits at 4.5% against the Bank of Japan at 1.25%, creating a 325bp nominal policy spread and a restrictive Norwegian real rate of +1.82% versus Japan's -2.25%. Macro data reinforces the bilateral gap, with Norway's Economic Surprise Index at +13.1 contrasting against Japan's -11.3. WTI crude trading firmly at $95.8 adds persistent terms-of-trade support to the krone while compounding imported energy drag on the yen. Trade bias: Long NOK/JPY, backed by wide policy rate spread and divergent macro surprises. Catalyst: Norges Bank meeting 5 Nov. Risk: Sharp risk-off shock unwinding cross carry trades.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Premium vs Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.44, holding above its SMA20 at 157.65 and SMA50 at 157.71 while testing the descending SMA200 at 158.48. OIS benchmarks show SOFR at 3.87% against TONA at 1.23%, delivering a +264bp carry advantage that structurally underpins spot demand. However, the options market displays intense hedging against a downside move, with 1M 25-delta risk reversals printing at -1.80, a strong put skew. Simultaneously, options implied volatility trades at 7.9% versus 30-day realized volatility of 9.7%, generating a negative volatility risk premium of -1.8%. That negative premium alongside extreme put skew indicates acute complacency in unhedged spot alongside institutional demand for downside tail protection. With 160.00 serving as the historical threshold for official Japanese verbal warnings, intervention sensitivity rises sharply on any sustained breakout above current resistance. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported above moving averages while capping upside expectations ahead of 160.00. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Core CPI printing below consensus, triggering immediate carry liquidation toward 157.65.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Short + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1198, remaining pinned below its SMA20 at 1.1327, SMA50 at 1.1492, and SMA200 at 1.1597. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds holding net short -84,775 contracts, sitting at the 4th percentile of the 52-week range with a z-score of -1.64. In the options space, 1M implied volatility trades at 6.5% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.2%, creating an elevated volatility risk premium of +2.3%. Rates drivers remain heavily tilted in the greenback's favor, with Fed at 4.00% versus ECB at 2.65% for a 135bp policy rate advantage, while the 20-day US 5-year yield move shows nominal +24bp with real yields contributing +33bp. This crowded speculative short setup leaves the pair vulnerable to sharp short-covering if macro data misses expectations. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, constrained by heavy real-yield headwinds but cautious on downside chasing into crowded shorts. Catalyst: US CPI release today at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Hot US core inflation print re-establishing aggressive downside momentum below 1.1150.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Carry Advantage + Headline Repricing
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7010, testing resistance directly below its SMA20 at 0.7016, SMA200 at 0.7040, and SMA50 at 0.7089. Fresh headline flow highlights Australian dollar strength fueled by market speculation over potential Reserve Bank of Australia tightening, with RBA at 4.60% against the Fed at 4.00% providing a 60bp cash carry advantage and an overnight AONIA-SOFR spread of +73bp in Australia's favor. Leveraged fund positioning reflects institutional demand with net long +48,911 contracts, representing 70.3% long open interest, yet weekly flow contracted by 6,203 contracts. Cross-asset volatility reveals the MOVE index elevated at 101.1, the 94th percentile of its trailing year, while VIX sits at 15.3, the 18th percentile. This divergence shows fixed-income markets pricing central bank path divergence that equity volatility has not reflected. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD, supported by positive carry and policy rate premium. Catalyst: Australia Employment Report tomorrow at 00:30 UTC. Risk: Australia unemployment rate rising unexpectedly, dampening RBA rate expectations.
evidence: RBA 4.60% vs Fed 4.00% — -60bp AUD carry premium
